title: 5a-1: LanguageAdapter trait + registry + pipeline dispatch
description:
## Parent

sutra/30 (PRD: core model redesign)

## What to build

Define the LanguageAdapter trait, LanguageRegistry, and wrap existing Rust/Dart parsers as concrete adapters. Wire the pipeline to dispatch via the registry instead of the match statement in parse_file().

This is a pure structural refactor -- no behavior change. Adapters still own tree-sitter internally, still produce flat ParseResult. The trait interface and registry are the foundation everything else builds on.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] LanguageAdapter trait defined with language_id(), extensions(), parse() methods and default as_fca_source() returning None
- [ ] LanguageRegistry holds registered adapters, dispatches by file extension
- [ ] RustAdapter wraps existing rust::parse(), DartAdapter wraps dart::parse()
- [ ] Pipeline (parse_workspace, parse_changed_files) uses LanguageRegistry for dispatch
- [ ] parse_file() free function removed or delegates to registry
- [ ] Behavioral parity: existing test suites pass, same symbols/refs/imports produced on test inputs
- [ ] Mock TestAdapter test verifying registration and dispatch
- [ ] Capability query test: as_fca_source() returns Some for Rust, None for minimal adapter

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex adversarial review — verdict: needs-attention

**Finding [medium]: Incremental parse ignores workspace language allowlist** (src/pipeline.rs:433-438)

`parse_changed_files` now sends every changed path through `parse_single_file`, which accepts any extension registered globally. Before the refactor, `parse_changed_files` built an `ext_to_lang` map from `workspace.languages`, so a Rust-only workspace would ignore a changed `.dart` file. With the new code, the default registry will parse and upsert that Dart file anyway.

Impact: incremental indexing can add files/languages the workspace did not opt into, producing different DB contents from a full parse and from the pre-refactor behavior. Behavioral parity claim is violated for this path.

Recommendation: Constrain registry dispatch by `workspace.languages` in `parse_changed_files` — e.g. build an allowed extension set from `registry.extensions_for_languages(&workspace.languages)` and filter before dispatching, or add a registry lookup that only considers the requested languages. Add a test where a Rust-only workspace receives a changed `.dart` file and verifies it is ignored.
